title: When the Atlas Falls
premise: In the river city of Vellamark, on the eve of the printers' revolution, Orsen Sandoval has passed as a man for twelve years in her father's type foundry, learning that silence is survival. When a census taker's probing question exposes her secret to the wrong ears, she discovers he is also carrying stolen census ledgers — proof the regime has been erasing thousands of 'unregistered' citizens, including her missing brother. Hunted by the Ministry of Records and betrayed by someone inside the print shop, Orsen must smuggle the ledgers past three checkpoints to the underground press before the city locks down. She reaches the press at terrible cost — her father dies holding the last checkpoint — but the Atlas edition prints overnight, and in its pages Orsen finally claims her own name, both of them, in ink.
about_author: Noor Eastwick is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal mill towns. Their fiction explores how ordinary workers carry history in their hands.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Orsen Sandoval, living as a man in her father's type foundry, sorts lead type while memorizing which questions never to answer. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the weary comfort of a carefully built double life, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: A census taker named Ivo Renner arrives for the annual count and asks about 'the Sandoval daughter, deceased?' Orsen lies smoothly, but Ivo's eyes linger. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into vigilance; the reader learns her brother Tomas vanished five years ago.

chapters.title: What the Foundry Remembers
chapters.summary: Father Aurel shows Orsen a hidden drawer of forbidden typefaces used by the old free presses. He hints he knows who she is without saying it. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: tenderness between father and child, built entirely on things unspoken.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counted People
chapters.summary: Ivo returns after hours, soaked in rain, and confesses he copied pages from the sealed census ledgers — names of thousands struck from the record, Tomas among them. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: his guilt curdling into purpose as he asks the foundry for help.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: The shop's compositors debate whether to help; master printer Halvard Voss refuses, citing the apprentices' safety. Orsen secretly agrees to hide the ledger pages in a font case. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge of Weighs
chapters.summary: Orsen carries the disguised pages across the customs bridge, talking her way past a guard who knew her as a boy. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: vertigo of passing — every identity she wears both shields and betrays her.

chapters.title: The Ministry of Records
chapters.summary: Clerk-Inspector Dame Saskia Mereau opens an inquiry into the missing ledger pages, suspecting Ivo. POV: Saskia. Emotional beat: cold competence masking a private doubt about the regime she serves.

chapters.title: Apprentice's Hands
chapters.summary: Young compositor Pellik notices Orsen's hidden pages and, terrified, tells Halvard — or so Orsen believes. Suspicion poisons the shop. POV: Pellik. Emotional beat: a boy's loyalty torn between fear and admiration.

chapters.title: Names Struck Through
chapters.summary: Reading the ledgers at night, Orsen finds Tomas's entry marked 'relocated' — the regime's word for disappeared. She grieves him properly for the first time. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Underground Press
chapters.summary: Ivo leads Orsen through the tannery district to the clandestine press run by Widow Anselma, a former typesetter. They agree to print the evidence as the 'Atlas Edition.' POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: first taste of found family among strangers bound by ink.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bitter Type
chapters.summary: Ministry agents raid the foundry following a tip; Halvard covers for Orsen and is taken for questioning. Orsen realizes the informant is still inside her circle. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: paranoia, and guilt that her father paid for her choice.

chapters.title: What Halvard Would Not Say
chapters.summary: Pellik confesses he told Halvard nothing — meaning the betrayal came from someone else, perhaps Ivo himself. Orsen confronts Ivo; he denies it, but doubt takes root. POV: Pellik. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being believed too late.

chapters.title: Saskia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Saskia interrogates Halvard and recognizes the foundry's typefaces from her childhood — her father was a printer erased from the rolls. POV: Saskia. Emotional beat: her certainty fractures; she begins quietly falsifying her own reports.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Salt Gate
chapters.summary: With the city under curfew, Orsen smuggles the full ledgers inside a shipment of type metal, nearly caught when a guard weighs the crate. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: nerve-shredding tension broken by an unexpected act of working-class solidarity.

chapters.title: The Face in the Census Book
chapters.summary: Anselma reveals a photograph attached to Tomas's file — alive, imprisoned in the Records House. Hope and horror arrive together. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous, almost unbearable weight.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ivo, waiting out a patrol, trade their secrets: his dead sister, her true name spoken aloud for the first time in years. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in danger; love neither will name yet.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Typeface
chapters.summary: Orsen identifies the informer by a distinctive ligature in a leaked document: it is Anselma's journeyman, Brann, selling pages to buy his family's registration. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: fury tempered by recognition — everyone breaks, given enough fear.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Records House
chapters.summary: To free Tomas and reach the final checkpoint, Orsen trades herself: she walks into the Records House wearing her truth openly for the first time. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: terror and liberation fused — hiding ends here.

chapters.title: The Lockdown of Vellamark
chapters.summary: Saskia, ordered to burn the seized evidence, instead misfiles it and unlocks a service door — then resigns her post in writing. POV: Saskia. Emotional beat: quiet, costly defection; conscience over career.

chapters.title: Atlas Falls
chapters.summary: At the last checkpoint, Aurel holds off the guards so the ledgers can pass, and is fatally shot in the foundry doorway. Orsen, escaping with Tomas, hears the bells toll the lockdown. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: devastating climax — victory purchased with her father's life.

chapters.title: The Morning Edition
chapters.summary: The Atlas Edition prints through the night; dawn finds every door in Vellamark papered with the erased names restored, Tomas's among them. The crowd reads itself back into existence. POV: multiple, brief. Emotional beat: catharsis — memory made public, irreversible.

chapters.title: Setting Her Name in Metal
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in the rebuilt foundry, Orsen cuts a new typeface and casts two words: her chosen name and her born one, side by side. Ivo stays; Pellik apprenticing; Saskia visits as a friend. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: resolution — identity not as a single truth but as a full set of type, hers to compose.
